clue.text: Author, female, so automatically slammed

indicators.note: something slammed is knocked about and battered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman writer pounds out her work on autopilot, perhaps savaged by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slammed' is the anagram signal working on all fifteen letters of SO AUTOMATICALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist who wrote Little Women was a woman, so 'Author, female' describes her.

clue.text: Socialist to change measure during recession

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist
to shift is to change or move

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician alters some economic yardstick while the country is in a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic, but here it is galaxies receding from us.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers gauge how fast a distant galaxy is moving away by how far its light is stretched toward longer wavelengths.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: taken in says the letters are held inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A drug addict is admitted to a clinic after slipping back into the habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug taker is commonly called a user, so an addict is one in everyday slang.

clue.text: Meet reformed son in shelter Tees needs to check

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it go inside the shelter word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind, as on the lee side of a wall

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of the word meet are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone meets a reformed son at a hostel; Tees, a man called by a river's name, must verify something.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter, so the definition is what he says when he must check: a phrase of hesitation. 'reformed' turns MEET into ETME, which with S goes 'in' LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person pausing to verify a detail typically says this phrase, so it captures someone needing to check.

clue.text: Be one about to lead nation

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the next word

parts.note: to run an organisation is to lead it
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An aspiring leader is told to be the one about to head the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sultanate on the island of Borneo is a sovereign state, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Party people making contribution to party funds?

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a nation is a people sharing a country

explanation.surface: Revellers hand over money to a political party's coffers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'party' in the definition is a political one while the first 'Party' is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift of money to a cause is a donation, and party funds are swelled by such gifts.

clue.text: Show Ben-Hur perhaps in empty depot

indicators.note: in says the film goes inside the remaining shell
empty means the word depot loses its inside letters, keeping only its outer pair

parts.note: Ben-Hur is a famous film epic, given by example with perhaps

explanation.surface: A cinema screening of Ben-Hur is staged in an abandoned warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something in a picture or description is to portray it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Land on Palaeozoic formations in LA?

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word lowlands are L and A, so LA is literally what sits at its centre

explanation.surface: A geology question about ancient rock formations in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles; it is the middle pair of letters of LOWLANDS. The region of Scotland between Highlands and Southern Uplands lies on Palaeozoic rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish rift valley sits on sedimentary and volcanic rocks laid down in the Palaeozoic era, so it is land on those formations.

clue.text: Drive carelessly flattening farm animal?

parts.note: run over is to flatten, so over can stand for flattening
a steer is a young castrated bull raised on a farm

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist runs down a bullock in a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: The whimsical reading is running over a steer; the real sense is a car turning more sharply than the driver intends.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying too much steering lock, so the car turns more sharply than intended, is a form of driving without due care.

clue.text: Alumnus feasted regularly, appearing thus?

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word feasted

explanation.surface: A former pupil who dined lavishly at reunions now looks the part.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: an old boy who keeps feasting ends up looking like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats lavishly over and over becomes very overweight, which is what the clue's picture implies.

clue.text: Fan must start in line to see player

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters that follow are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A supporter is told to begin queuing to watch a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like the supporter in the queue; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician performs on an instrument, so a player of one is the answer.

clue.text: Dry river — assistance needed to cross

indicators.note: to cross here means the help word stretches across the river letter, holding it

parts.note: aid is assistance or help

explanation.surface: A dried-up river means help is required to get across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Land without water is parched, and parched is dry, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Snake one absent-minded Italian lost in plant

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: lost means the Italian abbreviation drops out of the absent-minded word

parts.note: distrait means distracted or absent-minded

explanation.surface: A dreamy Italian loses a snake somewhere in his houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes IT out of DISTRAIT, leaving DISTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast-iron plant is a hardy foliage species, famously a Victorian parlour favourite.

clue.text: Lawman confiscates ecstasy from trashed Tyrolean teenager

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
confiscates means one letter is taken away from the fodder before mixing

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A law officer seizes the pills of a drunk young Austrian from the Tyrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confiscates' removes one E from TYROLEAN TEENAGER; 'trashed' rearranges the fifteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officer of the government is a senior lawyer, so a lawman in a high position.

clue.text: Our steel tempered and unyielding

indicators.note: tempered metal is reworked by heat, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A proud claim that a company's hardened steel will not bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm and determined will not give way, which is what unyielding means.

clue.text: What provides transparency, hiding no secret, ultimately?

definitions.text: What provides transparency, hiding no secret, ultimately?

indicators.note: hiding means the material holds the next word inside it

parts.note: glass is the see-through material that provides transparency

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word secret

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what offers openness while concealing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the Soviet policy of openness, which promised to keep no secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorbachev's policy of openness in the USSR aimed at transparency in government, keeping nothing secret.

clue.text: Scripture studies likely to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, the school subject once called Scripture
liable means likely, as in liable to happen

explanation.surface: Bible study is expected to be dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dependable can be counted on, which is what trustworthy means.

clue.text: American beans meal cooked for mariner

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A US-style dish of beans is prepared for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating in the merchant or Royal Navy with basic sea qualifications is a seaman, so a mariner.

clue.text: Dull London market with no room for meetings

indicators.note: with no means the meeting room is taken away from the market's name

parts.note: Leadenhall Market is a Victorian covered market in the City of London
a hall is a large room used for meetings

explanation.surface: A boring London market without any space for gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADENHALL Market is a covered market in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, grey and lifeless, like lead, so a dull sky or a dull performance.

clue.text: Engineer succeeded separating gold from another metal

indicators.note: separating means the letter goes between the two metals, splitting them

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
tin is another metal
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A metallurgist manages to part gold from a different metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert, later Lord, of that surname was the British engineer who founded a famous car maker.

clue.text: Piped down audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for down is heard, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: feeling down means feeling blue, sad

explanation.surface: A sad tune sounded out loud on the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped down' looks like a phrase for falling quiet; split it into 'Piped', the definition, and 'down', the word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to play a pipe, and playing a pipe means sending breath through it, past tense.

clue.text: Daily stories involving snide lad riled unhappy couple

indicators.note: involving means the cleaner and stories surround the mixed letters

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaner who comes in each day, in British usage
ana are collected anecdotes or stories about a person

indicators.note: riled means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper's gossip about a sneering youth provoked a miserable pair.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaning lady. 'riled' makes LESANDDI from SNIDE LAD, which CHAR...ANA 'involving' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince and Princess of Wales had a famously troubled marriage that ended in divorce in 1996.

clue.text: Almost committing murder

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: doing a crime is committing it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost committing murder' reads as an attempted killing; 'Almost' cuts the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill someone is slang, especially in crime fiction, a verb phrase meaning to murder.

clue.text: River runs through camping shelter

indicators.note: through means the letter passes into the middle of the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter used in camping
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A stream floods a campsite, flowing right through a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is one of England's major waterways, flowing through the Midlands to the Humber.

clue.text: Not out yet: news boss to be introduced

parts.note: in means not out, as of a batsman at the crease
still means yet, as in still to come
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A batsman still at the crease meets a newspaper editor being presented to him.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is 'not out' is still in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas gradually put into someone's mind have been implanted or brought in, so introduced.
